body: I do have a very neat usecase for this. Currently I'm building a spreadsheet application and to enable zooming (50 to 200 in steps of 10), dark/light theme toggle and active sheet highlight working for people not having JS enabled I'm having quite a bunch of links to the sheets in index.html. And with each sheet added the file gets substantily bigger due to the additional mappings needed to keep this working. If I could use multiple base elements then quite a junk of data could be saved. With only lines like the following, for three sheets it takes already 9256 chars...; 32 lines added per sheet. Excerpt: ```html ``` [...] ```html ``` It just needs to be designed in a way that it doesn't break basic site navigation for people using terminal web browser (lynx, w3m, links, elinks, chawan) cause those tend to be stuck in HTML4. (Edit: Apparently lynx can't cope with base tag at all but the others can at least, lol...) (Also ofc I could benefit from some other things, e. g. some shorter way to assign hashes or to having some html structure repeated with some upcounter for a number of links for example... feel free to mention this comment in other issues or message me per mail in case something might help me so I can keep watching out for that and adjust stuff as soon as it lands in modern browsers.)
